March 7 — Sunny<br><br>Today I played with Kenta in the park.<br><br>Kenta says he’s gonna move soon, but he’ll come<br>back when he’s older.<br><br>We promised to play in the park again together<br>when we grow up.
I doubt anyone will ever read this, but the memories<br>of my experiences are too much to bear alone, so I’ve<br>decided to confide in this diary.<br><br>I’m a nameless hacker. I infiltrate the networks of<br>huge corporations, steal their secrets, and sell them<br>to their rivals.<br><br>I already have more than enough money,
but it’s fun peering behind the scenes, so it’s almost<br>like a hobby for me.<br><br>I donate all the money I don’t use to things like<br>Pokémon conservation groups.<br><br>Ever since I was a kid, I’ve liked computers and<br>Pokémon more than people.
My field survey on Cinnabar proved quite fruitful.<br><br>I spoke with Pokémon Professors from other regions<br>and gained a number of insights for my own research.<br><br>Many folks were very concerned about possible<br>effects the recent weather disturbances may be<br>having on Pokémon.<br><br>On my way home, I found a young Tangela.
He appeared injured and weak, so I used a Potion<br>to heal him. He seemed to take a liking to me and<br>toddled along behind me.<br><br>I wasn’t sure what to do at first. I ended up bringing<br>him home with me, figuring he might be a good<br>playmate for my grandchild.
The sea is really rough today. The ship keeps swaying<br>back and forth. And swaying...and swaying...<br><br>It’s all I can do to write in this diary right now, but...<br>Ugh... I don’t feel so good... I might not be able to<br>write much mo—
It happened when I was hacking into a server in<br>another region for fun and stumbled on a system<br>with excessively high security.<br><br>Finding these sorts of things is always a thrill.<br>It took a lot of effort, but once I breached it,<br>all I could find was what seemed like trivial data<br>about weather patterns.<br><br>It was anticlimactic, but it made me think...
Why would someone put so much effort into hiding<br>something like this? That nagged at me.<br><br>So I dove back in. It took a lot of work, but I learned<br>how to make sense of the weather data. I was able to<br>gather that a natural disaster had struck that region—<br>dozens of huge, repeated hurricanes.<br><br>That’s the only conclusion I could draw, but I’d never<br>heard news about a disaster like that.
My grandchild plays with Tangela a lot these days.<br>They both seem to be having so much fun. Just<br>watching them warms my heart.<br><br>Tangela shows interest in any and all human activities.<br>When I’m working on the computer, he stares intently<br>at my screen with a curious expression.<br><br>Trainers who come to visit me also play with<br>Tangela, and...
Tangela seems intrigued by the items they use. He<br>looks enthralled by things like Pokédexes and<br>Poké Balls.<br><br>Are all Tangela brimming with curiosity?<br>Or is this little one just special?<br><br>Pokémon really are fascinating. There’s always more<br>to learn about them!
May 7<br>I can’t think of anything! I need to have FOUR design<br>proposals ready in two days, but I’m coming up blank!<br><br>I was begging my Smeargle for help, and he scribbled<br>some random patterns on a piece of paper and<br>handed it to me. Are those design pitches? That’s<br>so cute!<br><br>Actually...that gives me an idea. Back to work!
If a disaster of that scale had really happened,<br>surely it would have received both local and<br>global attention.<br><br>With that thought, I remembered a foundation active<br>in that region.<br><br>They were known for their passion for Pokémon<br>conservation efforts. I had even donated to them.<br>I thought that an organization of that scale
might be able to influence media so that no news of<br>the disaster leaked outside the region.<br><br>I spent countless days infiltrating the foundation’s<br>servers, looking into any data I could lay my hands<br>on. And sure enough, it gradually became clear that<br>they were involved.<br><br>I finally fell asleep after repeated all-nighters.<br>When I woke up, I was surrounded by members of<br>the foundation.
Apparently I’d left traces when I hacked the servers.<br>That was enough for them to track me down.<br><br>The people from the foundation were surprisingly<br>polite, and they explained what was happening<br>in detail.<br><br>I have no intention of writing it all here.<br><br>The important thing is that someday this disaster<br>will spread throughout the entire world.
They said that humanity in its current state can’t<br>prevent it.<br><br>The foundation, together with other regions, had<br>formed a plan to evacuate all of humanity into space.<br>The plan was already in motion. My head was<br>spinning at the outrageous tale.<br><br>So what would become of Pokémon? When I put the<br>question to them, they described their “Pokémon<br>Conservation Project” and asked for my help.
While humanity is evacuated into space, all of the<br>Pokémon in the world are to be stored and protected<br>in a massive computer system. That is the Pokémon<br>Conservation Project.<br><br>An incredible plan. But the foundation members said<br>that in order to avoid panic they had to keep both<br>the disaster and the project out of the public eye as<br>much as possible.<br><br>Naturally this left them shorthanded.
Skilled computer technicians were in particularly<br>high demand.<br><br>That’s why the foundation sought me out after I<br>discovered the disaster—recruitment.<br><br>I took them up on their offer.<br><br>Until this point, I had always lived as I pleased.<br>But if I could save Pokémon using my skills, I had<br>to do it.
The work was tough but also rewarding.<br><br>Eventually, the public began to take notice of the<br>disaster. The foundation gradually evacuated<br>those who noticed to a “safe place,” but to avoid<br>panic, they waited until the last minute to tell people<br>that their destination was space.<br><br>In the middle of this unbelievable situation, I found<br>a flaw in the plan.
In order to escape the disaster, humanity would<br>temporarily take refuge in space while Pokémon<br>would be safely stored in a computer system.<br>This was the general overview of the plan.<br><br>But no computer system will keep running forever.<br><br>The foundation planned to send a select few<br>members back to the planet at regular intervals to
perform ongoing maintenance.<br><br>But for humanity to survive in space for any length of<br>time, it would take a tremendous amount of energy.<br>I calculated that even a slight deviation from the<br>original plan would result in insufficient energy to<br>return, leaving humankind stranded in space for<br>dozens, or even hundreds, of years.<br><br>If that happened, the essential system protecting the<br>Pokémon would eventually cease to function.
So I decided to add a little touch of my own to the<br>system’s programming.<br><br>First, it will continuously check the weather data<br>across the globe in search of environments that can<br>prove even slightly habitable to Pokémon.<br><br>Next, if maintenance is not performed for a long<br>period of time and the system begins to approach<br>its limits, it will release the Pokémon most suited<br>to those environments.
Of course, ideally humans will return someday and<br>live alongside Pokémon once more.<br><br>But on the off chance humanity never returns from<br>space...I think releasing the Pokémon into a wild<br>world rather than leaving them asleep in a computer<br>would be a happier outcome.<br><br>It may sound strange coming from the program’s<br>creator, but I hope it never has to run.
Today there was a gathering attended by Pokémon<br>Professors from every region. We had a surprising<br>announcement in store.<br><br>Increasingly intense weather abnormalities—and the<br>calamities striking each region as a result—show no<br>sign of slowing down.<br><br>At this rate, predictions suggest that we will no<br>longer be able to obtain enough food and energy<br>to continue living on this planet.
And we learned that a plan was secretly in motion to<br>evacuate all of humanity into space.<br><br>It also seemed that, with a few exceptions, it will not<br>be possible to bring Pokémon with us.<br><br>Of course some immediately raised their voices in<br>protest, which is when we heard about the Pokémon<br>Conservation Project.
It was decided that we will take part in the Pokémon<br>Conservation Project.<br><br>It’s a plan to safely store all Pokémon on the planet<br>in a massive computer system while humanity takes<br>refuge in space.<br><br>I can’t be sure that such a thing is even possible,<br>and being parted from our Pokémon will be terribly<br>painful, but...
this may be the only way that people and Pokémon<br>will be able to live together again someday.<br><br>I was also asked to join a survey team after we move<br>to space, but I held off on responding.<br><br>After humanity relocates, a small group will be sent<br>back to the planet to survey the environment and do<br>maintenance on the conservation system. But given<br>my age, I don’t know if I’ll still be spry enough to be<br>of much help. I think it’s a task best left to the young.
Something shocking has happened.<br><br>The Pokémon Conservation Project is progressing<br>smoothly, and the time came for my Tangela to join<br>the others.<br><br>In the hopes of avoiding a tearful scene, I waited until<br>my grandchild was asleep before entrusting Tangela<br>to one of the other project members. But later that<br>night, I received word that Tangela had run off.
Tangela was like family. He should have been<br>accustomed to humans. How could this have<br>happened?<br><br>I have a theory.<br>Tangela was likely trying to get back to our home.<br><br>But it’s nearly time for my family to set off for space.<br>Even if Tangela were to make it safely home...
by the time he arrives, we’ll no longer be there.<br><br>I feel agonizingly helpless knowing there’s nothing I<br>can do.<br><br>Nothing, that is, but hope that the project staff find<br>Tangela and keep him safe...
The day of departure finally arrived, and Tangela was<br>still nowhere to be found.<br><br>So I decided to join the survey team after all.<br><br>It will give me the opportunity to return to the planet<br>periodically, and I can search when I’m there.<br><br>If there are any strange machines or rare tools on the<br>ship, I should borrow them.
Then I’ll find Tangela and show them to him.<br><br>I’m certain he’ll examine them with his usual curiosity.<br><br>Until then...please, be safe.
March 13<br><br>Charlotte appears to be interested in cooking! I tried<br>teaching her a bit, and she’s really quite good at it.<br>She’s very dexterous with those little Greedent<br>hands, and it took almost no time before she was<br>able to help me out with simple tasks.

What to do...

Changes due to downloadable content will take effect when you<br>visit your Cloud Island. If others are playing on the island at that<br>time, their sessions will end.
